output.summary: KEP-670 proposed building support for the out-of-tree vSphere cloud-controller-manager with feature parity to kube-controller-manager. The KEP is recorded as implemented at stage stable, a status set during a 2021 enhancements-tracking cleanup (PR #3007).
output.rationale: The KEP captures mostly implemented work already completed in the cloud-provider-vsphere repository, with the next step being migration of in-tree users to the external provider. Its status was set to implemented retroactively and was then debated in PR #3007 because the PRR (production readiness review) step was skipped. Sources do not record a final resolution of that PRR question for this KEP.

alternatives.option: Keep KEP-670 at implementable/alpha without a PRR-backed implemented status
alternatives.why_not: Sources say the KEP was retroactively declared beta and then implemented via PR #2598 and #2867 without PRR; the sources do not state this option was considered further.

alternatives.option: Treat the KEP as perma-beta (leave at beta indefinitely)
alternatives.why_not: A maintainer noted perma-beta is discouraged: 'we really shouldn't be leaving stuff in a perma-beta state.' This applied to a different KEP, and the sources do not apply it to KEP-670.

evidence.quote: This KEP captures mostly implemented work already completed in the [Cloud Provider vSphere repository]
The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle. Given that this KEP is related to prow
I think this is out of tree so maybe not explicitly covered by PRR
Generally "implemented" status comes after a kep was "implementable" as "stable" in a release and is updated after the fact and so should have a PRR.
